extracted.intended_audience: Navy/MSC managers, contracting officers, auditors, and personnel implementing OMB Circular A-76 for ship operations
extracted.subtask_short: OMB A-76 contracting implementation for ships
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evaluative standards for applying OMB Circular A-76 to determine whether MSC ship operations should be performed in-house or contracted out, including cost estimation, audit/review, solicitation, cost comparison, adjustments/differentials, decision, appeals, and implementation of the MEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house management reviews before calculating cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies to conduct in-house management reviews prior to calculating cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This will ensure that the operation is organized and staffed for consistency with the activity's manpower and personnel regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed cost-calculation procedures per Circular A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed procedures for calculation of material, personnel, and overhead costs along with standard formulas used to estimate retirement cost, insurance, workmen's compensation and other benefits are described in Circular A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Circular A-76 formulas and procedures when estimating material, personnel, overhead and benefits costs for the in-house estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review/audit of in-house estimate, SOW, and MEO
rubrics_metrics.description: After the in-house estimate is prepared it must be reviewed by a qualified activity, usually by an independent audit agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The area Naval Audit Service normally performs this service for Navy commands, ensuring compliance with A-76. The Audit Service also reviews and approves the proposed Statement of Work (SOW) and the Most Efficient Organization (MEO). This audit must be started 120 days prior to bid opening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation follows approved in-house estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: When the in-house estimate has been approved, contract bids or proposals will be solicited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although firm fixed-price contracts are the preferred method of contracting, other pricing arrangements and formal advertising may be approved in rare instances. Sealed bids submitted by the government and potential contractors are opened and costs compared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract bid opening and lowest acceptable determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The contracting officer opens the bids on the appointed date and determines the lowest acceptable contract price of the responsive and qualified bidders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only responsive and qualified bids are considered when determining the lowest acceptable contract price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling no-bid situations
rubrics_metrics.description: If no contractors bid, work goes directly to the government. If there is no government bid, a contractor is selected to perform the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural fallback when one side does not submit a bid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award survey threshold (90% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the lowest contract price appears to be sufficiently less costly (less than 90 percent of the government cost), a pre-award survey is conducted to determine if the lowest bidder is capable of performing the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the pre-award survey finds the bidder capable, the contract is awarded and the in-house operation is dismantled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government performance when bids exceed threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: If all contract bids exceed 90 percent of the in-house cost, then the government performance is noted as the lowest bid and the cost comparison process is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No conversion to contract performance if bids are not sufficiently lower than in-house estimate per the 90% rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of differentials/adjustments in cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular A-76 provides for the use of differentials in considering conversions of either in-house or contract performance when the contract price is less than the in-house estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments are made to the in-house bid to consider the cost of a capital charge that may be added if government assets are required to assure contract performance. The lowest bid contract price is also adjusted to consider several factors: a cost of capital charge when government assets are required to insure contractor performance; conversion costs to reflect one-time costs incurred by the government in switching operations from in-house to contract; additional overhead to be absorbed when an activity experiences a reduction of present capacity due to contracting out; and deduction of the potential federal income tax revenue that would be paid by the contractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion savings threshold (10% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An existing in-house function will not be converted to contract performance unless the conversion will result in savings of more than 10 percent of the government estimated personnel related cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This (cost) differential is included to account for the possible loss of production, the temporary decrease in efficiency and effectiveness, and other unpredictable risks that result from contract conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision, approval, public notice, and appeal timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of the cost comparison process, a recommendation is made to either award the contract or perform the function in-house and forwarded to the approving authority for review and approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once approved, results of the cost study are announced and detailed analysis made available to the public. If no significant discrepancies are identified or an appeal lodged within 5 working days (which may be extended by the contracting officer up to 15 days for complex decisions), the contracting officer will either award the contract or cancel the solicitation. In the event the function is to be performed in-house, implementation of the MEO must be initiated within 30 days and be completed within one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost minimization as primary decision criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Circular A-76 states a philosophical preference for using commercial sources whenever possible, it mandates cost minimization as the criterion for deciding whether government employees or private sector contractor should perform functions that are not intrinsically governmental in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions to convert to contract performance should be driven by demonstrable cost savings according to A-76 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Efficiency Studies (MES) mandatory
rubrics_metrics.description: The commercial activity management (cost) study is mandatory under Circular A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The activity must use the criteria of the study and cost comparison to determine the most efficient organization. The government in-house estimates are then based on achieving the MEO. MES data (e.g., proposed manning reductions, use of labor-saving capital equipment like cafeteria feeding facilities and automatic data processing machines) inform the cost comparison and proposed organizational changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFP/SOW/MEO staffing standards and minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: RFPs recommended the elimination of all positions over the required industry or Coast Guard minimum. When these minimums differ, Coast Guard requirements took precedence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions recommended for elimination included Stewards, Cooks-Bakers, 2nd Assistant Engineers, Unlicensed Junior Engineers, Laundrymen, Messmen, Yeomen/Storekeepers and Radiomen; engineering and steward departments often took largest cuts. Operational changes (e.g., Night Mates/Engineers on weekends; converting dayworkers to watchstanders; using contract guard service in port) were recommended to accommodate reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage and labor cost baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: The wage rates used in MSC cost estimate are the wage determinations for Civil Service mariners made by the U.S. Department of Labor under the Service Contract Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors negotiate wages with the labor union for each position on a specified ship type; these amounts vary with each union. Wage-scale differences and contractor-paid insurance premiums affect cost comparisons; e.g., MSC studies show use of Civil Service personnel is 20 percent less expensive than use of contract manning (excluding premium pays).

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance requirements for contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: The RFP stipulates that the contractor shall secure the customary full form Protection and Indemnity (P&I) marine insurance coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insurance is to cover all liabilities in the amount of $100 million per incident; the contractor shall be responsible for the cost of the insurance, including deductibles. The annual insurance premium for contracted ships should be estimated and included in cost comparisons.
